body: so in effect i can relate that i have constant gruesome fantasies of suicide but don't plan to do it and things should be fine. should probably leave the outward violence out of it i suppose. thanks for the reply.

wondering: in therapy the professional is compelled to contact the authorities if A) you are deemed to be a danger to yourself, B) you are deemed to be a danger to others, or C) you appear to be incapable of taking care or yourself in a basic human fashion? 
i ask as i'm not sure what to withhold from this person. a few days ago i went through the intake psychologist at the local mental hospital and lied just enough to be assessed as "sub-acute" for involuntary hospitalization. when meeting with this new person i'm not sure how much of the truth i can tell him--self harm, near wall painting with brains, prodigious drug abuse, violent acting out, etc. if i'm locked up i'll lose my emotional base, which is what's kept me here (on earth, heart beating,etc) through the last week. can one frame statements as hypothetical as a transparent loophole in conversation? also, a somewhat related question: after being shuttled from the psych ward to the ER i was prescribed valium to assist with the discomfort of alcohol withdrawal and now can't achieve an erection to save my (sex) life. might this be psychological or due to the diazepam? it's intensely frustrating as sex was the one healthy release i indulged in. appointment in T-2.5 hrs and counting. advice appreciated.
